claims.claim: The reference solution passes all 11 acceptance tests, and each of five deliberate defects (overwrite on bronze, missing tracker in the gold grain, unfiltered silver waves, cast instead of try_cast, no source dedup before MERGE) fails at least one test.
claims.source: Local run on PySpark 4.0.4 and delta-spark 4.0.1, September 2026.

concept_html:
This capstone brings Track A together. You start from practice/capstone/before_pipeline.py: a notebook exported as one script, the way many pipelines begin. It runs, and it breaks almost every rule in CLAUDE.md. You finish with practice/exercises/x1_pipeline.py, refactored to the standard and passing 11 acceptance tests on a local SparkSession.

What the starting code gets wrong (each one is a lesson you have done):

  • A SparkSession created at import time, and a hard-coded column map (A1).
  • Bronze written with mode("overwrite"), and counted before the write (A2).
  • No missing-column check before renames, and casts that hide bad values (A2, D3).
  • A MERGE with no deduplication of the source (A3).
  • A gold groupBy that drops tracker_id, a sum(when(...)) that gives null, and an unguarded division (A5, D4).
  • Checks stored as text in a mutable default list, with repeated count() calls (A6, D3).
  • A run log with no schema, uuid and datetime never imported, and utcnow() (A7, D1).
  • A secret placeholder in code (A10).

What you deliver: ten functions with fixed names and signatures, listed in the skeleton. The acceptance tests in practice/tests/test_x1_pipeline.py import them. They check behaviour, not style, so run ruff and mypy as well.

How to work. Read the brief and the tests first. Implement one function at a time, in the order of the pipeline: config, bronze, silver, gold, checks, run log. Run the tests after each function. Compare with practice/solutions/x1_pipeline.py only once your tests pass.

The exercises below practise the pure-Python parts in the browser. The Spark parts run on your laptop. Setup is in practice/README.md.

exercises.solution:
REQUIRED_CONFIG_KEYS = (
    "tracker_id",
    "column_map",
    "type_map",
    "merge_keys",
    "weight_sum_min",
    "weight_sum_max",
    "max_null_weights",
)


def validate_config(raw: dict[str, object]) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Check a pipeline config before any step uses it.

    Args:
        raw: Parsed JSON config.

    Returns:
        The same config, if valid.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If keys are missing or values are impossible.
    """
    missing = [key for key in REQUIRED_CONFIG_KEYS if key not in raw]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"config is missing keys: {missing}")
    if not raw["merge_keys"]:
        raise ValueError("merge_keys must not be empty")
    if float(raw["weight_sum_min"]) > float(raw["weight_sum_max"]):  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        raise ValueError("weight_sum_min exceeds weight_sum_max")
    return raw

exercises.solution:
def enforce(results: list[dict[str, str]]) -> None:
    """Stop the pipeline when a CRITICAL check failed.

    Args:
        results: Structured check results.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: Naming every failed CRITICAL check.
    """
    failed = [
        r["check_name"] for r in results if r["severity"] == "CRITICAL" and r["status"] == "FAIL"
    ]
    if failed:
        raise RuntimeError(f"CRITICAL checks failed: {failed}")

exercises.solution:
import uuid
from datetime import datetime, timezone


def build_run_record(
    pipeline_name: str,
    tracker_id: str,
    wave_id: str,
    layer: str,
    rows_processed: int,
    status: str,
    error_message: str | None = None,
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """One run log record with a new run id and an aware UTC timestamp.

    Args:
        pipeline_name: Job name, such as nat_silver_pipeline.
        tracker_id: Tracker processed.
        wave_id: Wave processed.
        layer: bronze, silver or gold.
        rows_processed: Rows written by the run.
        status: Outcome of the run.
        error_message: Error text for a failed run.

    Returns:
        The record, ready for a schema-typed append.
    """
    return {
        "run_id": str(uuid.uuid4()),
        "pipeline_name": pipeline_name,
        "tracker_id": tracker_id,
        "wave_id": wave_id,
        "layer": layer,
        "rows_processed": rows_processed,
        "status": status,
        "error_message": error_message,
        "run_timestamp": datetime.now(timezone.utc),
    }

title: Capstone 1: refactor the NAT pipeline
why_html: Refactoring a working pipeline is harder than writing a new one. The old code produces numbers people rely on, and every change risks moving them. Acceptance tests with known answers let you change structure without changing results. This is how you will improve real pipelines at work: one tested function at a time, never a rewrite in one go.
